label: churn200-s6
summary: This churn model (training AUC 0.919) is a sum of seven parts on the score scale, passed through a sigmoid. Its strongest part is a customer-service-call alarm gated by usage: of the training customers with 4 or more service calls, the 122 with low or average daytime spending (usage level off) have a churn rate of 91.8% and a mean predicted risk of 82.5%, while the 196 heavy daytime spenders have a churn rate of 24.0% and a mean predicted risk of 25.0%; switching the alarm off lowers the AUC to 0.812. The international plan enters through a direct edge of 0.86 per sd and raises the typical customer's predicted risk from 1.3% to 20.2%. Two usage hinges add risk for heavy users: one for high daytime spending without voicemail messages (acting on 1077 customers, churn rate 26.9%), one for heavy combined day and evening use (acting on 805 customers, churn rate 33.9%). State gates give a few states their own offset, the largest for New Jersey (90 customers, churn rate 24.4%); these are fitted to small groups. An evening-charge hinge is a small counterweight. At 3 service calls the alarm fires for 198 customers whose churn rate is 6.6% against a mean predicted risk of 14.7%, an over-prediction worth checking.

resisted: The state gates are described more than explained: the model gives New Jersey, Washington and Iowa their own offsets, but nothing in the inputs says why, and Iowa's positive offset goes against its training churn rate of 10.9% (55 customers). The evening-charge hinge pulls against the observed churn rate of the customers it acts on (18.0% against 12.9%) and reads as an offset to the day-evening hinge rather than a signal of its own.

Splits are all on input nodes (-71,-61,-64,-59,-30,-26,-42,-44); cross-part hidden edges (20866->4397, 10379->7689, 1694->997, 4397->997) are carried by identity nodes so no hidden node is split; identity_direct and identity_state gather the direct edges and the state gates at the output.
tool_bugs: (1) Placeholders cannot reference probe input values whose variable name has a space (rows[k].inputs.total day charge exists in the stored values, but the placeholder regex has no space), and the render leaves them silently unrendered with no error; probe settings (e.g. 4 calls, 35 US dollars) were therefore written as allow_numbers literals. (2) xn.py --render takes no allow list, so the summary's literals '4' and '3' (service-call counts used as subgroup definitions) show as render errors although they are constructed settings, not computed values. (3) add_evidence has no allow_numbers, so evidence narratives with a count in a label were refused and re-added with the count in words. (4) An annotation's entry nodes count as covered, so a hidden exit of one leaf cannot be the entry of another; worked around with identity nodes on the receiving edges.
